analysis.investment_thesis: All Time Plastics is a freshly-listed IPO (equity jumped from ₹202 Cr to ₹594 Cr in 2025, indicating fresh issue proceeds) trading at 36.5x earnings and 1.88x book — well beyond my quantitative thresholds. While the balance sheet is respectable and earnings are growing, the price embeds speculative assumptions with no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.22 and post-IPO capital infusion leave the balance sheet conservative
Four consecutive years of positive operating cash flow (27→67→91→52 Cr)
ROE of 19% and 3-yr net profit CAGR of 24% show genuine earnings growth, not just promise
key_risks: P/E 36.5 and P/B 1.88 fail my thresholds (<15 and <1.5); Graham Number ≈ ₹133 vs price ₹217 — no margin of safety
Recent IPO — lacks the multi-year track record as a listed entity; investment bankers priced this for sellers
FY2025 FCF turned negative ₹62 Cr on ₹114 Cr capex, suggesting growth is consuming capital
red_flags: IPO premium pricing — equity base tripled in 2025 reflecting fresh issue at elevated multiples
No evident dividend record as a listed company
Commodity plasticware is a low-moat, competitive business; 10% operating margin is unremarkable
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The stock fails nearly every quantitative filter I demand. P/E of 36.5x is more than double my ceiling of 15; P/B of 1.88 exceeds my 1.5 limit; and the Graham Number test — sqrt(22.5 × EPS ₹7.9 × BVPS ₹100) ≈ ₹133 — shows the intrinsic value anchor sits 39% below the market quote of ₹217. There is no margin of safety here. The balance sheet is the one redeeming feature: D/E 0.22, total debt ₹223 Cr against ₹594 Cr of equity, and interest coverage (EBITDA ₹102 Cr / finance cost ₹15 Cr ≈ 6.8x) is adequate.

The business itself — molded plastic household goods under the "alltime" brand since 1964 — is prosaic and competitive, with 10% operating margins suggesting limited pricing power. Earnings growth is real (net profit ₹25→₹47 Cr over three years), but this is precisely what speculators pay 36x for and what Mr. Market inevitably disappoints on. FY2025 FCF went to negative ₹62 Cr as capex accelerated, financed by the IPO proceeds. As always with IPOs, the seller knows more than the buyer — I would require the price to fall below ₹130 and demand a 3-5 year listed earnings record before considering this. AVOID.
